guide.title: Field Manual
guide.subtitle: From province armies to the seven-resource economy, policy and diplomacy — everything on one page.
guide.footNote: Tip: you can reopen this manual at any time with the ? button in the top right.
guide.section.basics.label: Basics
guide.section.basics.lead: A campaign begins with a click on the map. Start with selection, movement and turn resolution.
guide.step.viewSelect.title: Viewing & Selecting
guide.step.viewSelect.body: The top resource bar shows the turn count, season and resources; the tabs below (Armies/Build/Policy/Diplomacy/Trade/Expansion) collapse via «. Clicking a tile shows its province and state; the Armies tab then shows its composition and can set stance or clear field troops. The badge on the map is that province’s field army — it grows with every regiment and shows the majority unit glyph; hover a province for population, army capacity and garrison. Press Esc, right-click or ✕ to clear the selection. State mode hides province armies, garrisons and battle marks and shows an aggregated state snapshot on hover.
guide.step.mapTint.title: Map Tinting
guide.step.mapTint.body: National borders are thick dark lines and provincial borders are lighter. Click the gear at the top right to open the settings menu: Tint Mode switches between Uniform (every province of a nation shares one depth) and Gradient (the default: zooming out past the dark threshold deepens the whole nation, while zooming in keeps it light and adds a national-colour outline just inside the border to highlight the front). The Dark Threshold slider adjusts the trigger live, and Restore Defaults resets everything. Settings save automatically; press Esc or click outside the menu to close it.
guide.step.moveMerge.title: Recruiting & army badges
guide.step.moveMerge.body: Drag a unit button onto one of your provinces to raise a regiment instantly; keep hovering the same province for 2 seconds to keep recruiting until you release or run out of resources or cap. The province shows its majority unit type and the badge grows with its regiments; recruiting uses the national army cap, never population.
guide.step.splitGroup.title: Composition & clearing
guide.step.splitGroup.body: The army tab lists the province composition and can clear its field troops, leaving only the local garrison; drag new units to rebuild. The national cap comes from population, conscription share and a coefficient.
guide.step.multiDayMarch.title: Stances & coordination
guide.step.multiDayMarch.body: Each province can be auto (attack only when stronger), defend (passive only) or attack (seek the weakest neighbour). Provinces aimed at the same target attack together without moving troops, grinding down and capturing under-defended land.
guide.step.endTurn.title: Ending the Turn
guide.step.endTurn.body: Press E or click End Turn at the top right. AI actions, battle resolution, marches, production, training and supply recovery are all settled within one [[turn]], then the next [[turn]] begins.
guide.step.shortcuts.title: Shortcuts
guide.step.shortcuts.body: E / Space: End turn · M: Toggle sound · Esc: Cancel selection or strategic redeployment · Right-click: Cancel selection.
guide.section.combat.label: Province armies
guide.section.combat.lead: Troops live in their province and stack into an army; provinces attack by stance and trade casualties with the garrison.
guide.step.armiesUnits.title: Province armies & units
guide.step.armiesUnits.body: Each unit stays in the province where it is raised and uses the national army cap (population × conscription share × coefficient) instead of population. Infantry is cheap, tanks are mobile, artillery sieges well. Damaged units recover each [[turn]] when [[supply]] is sufficient.
guide.step.organization.title: [[organization]]
guide.step.organization.body: [[organization]] (0–100) scales that province army's attack and defense and recovers each [[turn]] with [[supply]]. Coordinated provinces keep their own organization.
guide.step.battle.title: Contesting provinces
guide.step.battle.body: An attacking province fights a neighbour every [[turn]]: attack power is compared with the [[garrison]] and field defense, and both sides take casualties. Once the garrison and defenders are gone the province is captured and half the surviving attackers stay to hold it.
guide.step.garrison.title: [[garrison]]
guide.step.garrison.body: Every province has a [[garrison]] generated from its output, city level and terrain. In an active war, a province with no [[garrison]] and no defenders can be occupied outright. A [[fort]] only strengthens that province's [[garrison]]: +50% cap, recovers 15% of the cap per turn outside combat (normally 10%), deals 25% more damage and takes 0.8× damage; it does not raise terrain or city [[defense]] multipliers.
guide.step.redeploy.title: Province Stance & Clearing
guide.step.redeploy.body: Each province can be set to Auto, Defend or Attack: Defend only takes hits, Attack pushes into neighbouring provinces, and Auto only strikes with a clear advantage. Clear field troops to keep the garrison; the composition rows also let you disband one regiment per type.
guide.step.supply.title: [[supply]]
guide.step.supply.body: Capitals, cities and provincial [[supply]] centers provide [[supply]]. A [[supply]] center costs [[construction:30]] and takes a while to build; it radiates 8 tiles through your land, with u = 1 − d/8 at distance d, adding +10u percentage points of [[supply]] and a ×(1 + 0.2u) multiplier; overlapping sources take the strongest value rather than stacking. [[supply]] can exceed 100%, but combat and [[organization]] recovery only count up to 100%; below 50%, reinforcements stop, and low [[occupation]] shortens the reach of city and capital [[supply]].
guide.section.economy.label: Economy & Construction
guide.section.economy.lead: Seven resources drive the war machine: [[funds]], [[manpower]], [[industry]], [[politics]], plus [[raw]], [[food]] and [[strategic]]; [[stability]] runs through production, [[politics]] and manpower.
guide.step.resources.title: Resource Overview
guide.step.resources.body: [[funds]] comes from provincial taxes (cities pay in full, non-city provinces about a fifth), [[farm]]s and [[production]][[factory]]s, and pays for recruiting, construction and army upkeep; [[armyUnits]] is army capacity: cap = population × conscription share × coefficient, with occupied population weighted by [[occupation]] — raising troops uses the cap, never population; [[industry]] comes from cities and [[production]][[factory]]s and pays for recruiting, replacements and buildings; [[politics]] gives +2 per [[turn]] plus +1 per [[admin]], spent on policy switches, state claims and war-goal preparation. Unpaid armies lose [[organization]] every [[turn]].
guide.step.rawFoodStrategic.title: Raw Materials / Food / Strategic Resources
guide.step.rawFoodStrategic.body: [[raw]] and [[strategic]] come from provincial mines scattered by terrain (a province may have none, one or two), with output = mine level × 1.5 × (60% + 10% per [[infrastructure]] level) × [[occupation]]. [[production]][[factory]]s consume [[raw]] and a little [[strategic]]; tanks and artillery consume [[strategic]] each turn and all armies eat [[food]]. [[food]] comes from provincial base output and [[farm]]s and feeds the population and armies: the population is fairly stable and surplus food grows it only very slowly; a shortage halts growth, gradually shrinks the population and lowers [[stability]], while mines lose up to 99%. When net surplus exceeds 25% of output, population growth gets an extra +20%. Net changes and shortages are calculated each turn, then stocks and population update in one pass. Shortages also reduce army [[organization]].
guide.step.trainingDeploy.title: Recruiting & Deployment
guide.step.trainingDeploy.body: Drag a unit type from the Armies tab onto a map province; the regiment forms there immediately, and hovering the same province for 2 seconds keeps recruiting. Each costs [[funds]] and [[industry]] and counts against the national army cap. The cap scales with population, conscription policy and a coefficient, with occupied population weighted by [[occupation]]; recruits no longer consume population. Clear field troops or disband single regiments to free cap.
guide.step.buildingsOwnership.title: Six Buildings & Ownership
guide.step.buildingsOwnership.body: [[factory]]s, [[farm]]s, [[infrastructure]] and [[admin]] are built at state level; [[supply]] centers and [[fort]]s are built in a specific province. Regional bonuses are unified per state rather than stacking province by province: economic and area bonuses are managed by the state, while [[supply]] reach and [[garrison]] protection stay local. Each state allows as many [[factory]]s and [[farm]]s as it has provinces, counting both built and queued ones; only one [[admin]] per state, providing just [[politics:+1]]/[[turn]].
guide.step.stateInfrastructure.title: State [[infrastructure]]
guide.step.stateInfrastructure.body: [[infrastructure]] level L = 0–8: output and construction multipliers are both 0.8 + 0.05L, movement cost is 1 − 0.05L and the [[supply]] multiplier is 1 + 0.05L. At level 0 these are 0.8/0.8/1/1, and at level 8, 1.2/1.2/0.6/1.4. It only applies to provinces still held by the same nation as the state center; provinces under another owner count as level 0.
guide.step.constructionQueue.title: [[construction]] & the National Queue
guide.step.constructionQueue.body: Buildings consume [[construction]] rather than a fixed number of turns. The queue assigns [[idle]][[factory]]s in order, up to 5 per project, with spare [[factory]]s going to the next one; each provides 0.5 base points per [[turn]] × the source state's output multiplier × the target state's construction multiplier (both 0.8 + 0.05L). With no [[idle]][[factory]], work pauses. Drag to reorder priorities; canceling refunds half of the [[funds]] and [[industry]] already paid. When a project finishes, [[factory]]s are reassigned from the next turn and are not spent again in the current [[turn]].
guide.step.buildMapLayers.title: Build Map & Layers
guide.step.buildMapLayers.body: In Build, first pick a state or province building icon, then click your own land state or province on the map to queue it; you can pick several sites in a row. Map shading shows (built + in progress) / cap: light when free, a distinct darkest shade when full, with an intermediate gradient for state buildings. Each province allows one [[supply]] center and one [[fort]], queued ones included, and you do not need to control the state center; land and water outside your control are neither shaded nor buildable. Province capacity numbers appear when you zoom in; zoomed out, only shading shows, and the province layer does not summarize state buildings. Insufficient resources still block queuing. Right-click or Esc cancels the selection, switching building tiers clears it, and closing the Build page restores the normal map; army badges on the map will not steal siting clicks, and the army list on the right can still take command.
guide.step.stateFactoryAllocation.title: States & [[factory]] Allocation
guide.step.stateFactoryAllocation.body: At the start, states are laid out and every land state is assigned to a nation: the mainland expands evenly by province count, leftovers join the nearest neighbouring nation, overseas states go wholly to the nation with the closest coast, and no neutral territory exists. Each state centers on a city; in war, actual control is contested province by province, and capturing a state center only changes that province's control and access to state buildings, not other provinces or formal ownership. Each [[production]][[factory]] yields per [[turn]] a base [[funds:+2]] and [[industry:+2]], scaled by the source state's output multiplier; [[idle]][[factory]]s feed the national construction queue. Scroll up in the top [[factory]] allocation bar for more [[production]], down for more [[idle]]; once focused, you can also use arrow keys or +/−.
guide.step.occupation.title: [[occupation]]
guide.step.occupation.body: Captured non-core provinces start integrating at 0%, gaining a base +4 per [[turn]], modified by occupation policy; [[admin]] does not speed it up. Efficiency determines that province's output and [[supply]] passage: output starts at 25% and reaches full effect at 100%. Historical core provinces (starting territory) become fully effective as soon as they are retaken; claiming, occupying or formally ceding a province never turns a non-core into a historical core.
guide.section.diplomacy.label: Policy & Diplomacy
guide.section.diplomacy.lead: Every province on the map already belongs to a nation, with no neutral territory. Claim land and prepare first, then go to war over a target; there are no factions or complex conferences.
guide.step.policies.title: Policies
guide.step.policies.body: The Policy tab uses compact horizontal buttons to switch three groups: economy ([[funds]]/[[industry]] bias), conscription (recruitable share and stability modifier versus [[funds]]), and occupation (integration speed and tax revenue from occupied land). Hover a button for exact bonuses; each switch costs [[politics:20]] and takes effect immediately. Total War suits decisive battles, while lenient occupation helps digest new territory quickly.
guide.step.stability.title: [[stability]]
guide.step.stability.body: [[stability]] is a nationwide 0–100 state starting at 65, moving at most 1.2 toward its target each [[turn]]. Target = 55 + 1.5 per [[admin]] (cap +15) − 5 per war + conscription modifier (volunteer 0 / conscript -5 / total war -10) − 0.3 per non-core province (cap -10), +5 for a [[food]] surplus or -10 for a shortage. Declaring war costs both sides 4 (the aggressor another 4), and making peace gives both sides 5. Stability scales [[funds]]/[[industry]]/[[raw]]/[[strategic]]/[[food]] output (×0.8 + 0.2 × stability/100), [[politics]] income (×0.5 + 0.5 × stability/100) and [[manpower]] replenishment (× stability/100).
guide.step.ownership.title: Formal Ownership, Control & Cores
guide.step.ownership.body: Actual control of a province determines current garrisons and actions, while legal ownership sets war goals and peace concessions. Wartime occupation only changes actual control; it does not turn another nation's land into your formal territory. Historical cores are set by starting ownership; a state claim is only a political demand, not a core, and grants no automatic right to attack.
guide.step.diplomacyPage.title: Diplomacy Page & Nation Cards
guide.step.diplomacyPage.body: The Diplomacy tab focuses on relations between nations: hover [i] next to the heading for campaign goals and rules; the top shows live annexation progress, ongoing wars and ready war goals; the nation colour blocks below are target tabs, with name, status and size on hover — a red ring means at war, a yellow ring means a truce. The detail card lists army unit count and actually controlled states/provinces vertically, with a row of Diplomatic Actions below: Prepare War Goal (shown as Stop Preparing while counting down) opens a centered action menu, where you can check an existing claim to prepare a Conquest goal, choose Full Annexation, or check a project in progress to cancel it — canceling refunds the creation cost but not the per-turn upkeep already spent, and takes effect on confirmation. Ask for Peace is available only during a war. Once a goal is ready, click Declare War (hover for prerequisites), pick a war goal in the dialog and confirm to actually start the war. When your goal is met you can Enforce Goal to settle peace as agreed.
guide.step.expansionPage.title: Expansion Page & Claim Management
guide.step.expansionPage.body: The Expansion tab manages state claims on its own and switches to state mode as soon as you open it: hover [i] to the right of the heading for all claim rules. The page only lists states you have already claimed, for management (cancel, locate, focus); it no longer lists claimable targets. Claimable states flash a golden outline along their borders on the map; click one to spend [[politics:{{cost}}]] on a claim, click it again to cancel and get the political power back (not allowed during a war). Claimed states are filled in your national colour with their borders outlined; clicking a list entry focuses the outline, Locate centers the map on the state, and Esc clears the focus. War goals are prepared in the Diplomatic Actions menu on the Diplomacy tab.
guide.step.stateHoverSnapshot.title: State Hover Snapshot
guide.step.stateHoverSnapshot.body: In state map mode, hovering motionless for 800ms opens a whole-state summary: cores (historical core nations), owner (formal owner), control breakdown (each nation's actual percentage) and nations holding claims, all shown as colour-coded nation tags. The snapshot is computed once when the hover begins and does not refresh live while shown; move the mouse away or pan the map and hover again to recompute it.
guide.step.claimsWarGoals.title: State Claims & War Goals
guide.step.claimsWarGoals.body: Claims can only be made from the Expansion tab or the map in state mode: the target state must contain another nation's formal territory and border you or hold one of your historical cores, then costs [[politics:{{claimCost}}]]. The Conquest goal additionally costs [[politics:{{conquestCost}}]], needs [[turn:{{conquestDays}}]] of preparation (upkeep each [[turn]]: [[politics:{{conquestUpkeep}}]]), stays ready for [[turn:{{conquestValidDays}}]], and requires the target state to be claimed. Full Annexation needs no state claim: it costs [[politics:{{annexCost}}]], [[turn:{{annexDays}}]] of preparation (upkeep each [[turn]]: [[politics:{{annexUpkeep}}]]) and is valid for [[turn:{{annexValidDays}}]]. You can declare war only when a valid goal is ready and the truce has ended; declaring consumes the goal, and canceling a claim invalidates its Conquest goal.
guide.step.preparationQueue.title: Preparation Queue & Deadlines
guide.step.preparationQueue.body: Each nation can have at most one diplomatic preparation still counting down at a time; different goals that are already ready can coexist. A war goal requires peace with the target and an ended truce; a Conquest goal must neighbor the chosen state, and an Annexation goal must border the target nation. Canceling a project that is still counting down in the Diplomatic Actions menu refunds its creation cost, but per-turn upkeep already spent is not returned; abandoning a ready or expired goal gives nothing back. The conditions for claims and goals still depend on current territory and diplomacy; an expired goal cannot be used to declare war and must be prepared again.
guide.step.enforceWarGoals.title: Enforcing War Goals
guide.step.enforceWarGoals.body: Conquest of a claimed state: once you fully control the target's formal territory inside that state, click Achieve War Goal to take those provinces. Full annexation: control the capital and at least 60% of formal territory with no third-party occupation, or control all of the target's formal territory. The fall of a capital alone does not destroy a nation. Temporary occupation outside the goal is returned at peace, and land cannot be handed over to a third country through concessions.
guide.step.whitePeace.title: White Peace & Withdrawal
guide.step.whitePeace.body: You can propose a white peace during a war; the AI accepts or rejects based on the situation and may itself sue for peace when losing. A white peace keeps no temporary occupations: both sides return occupied areas and no third-country land changes hands. Either a white peace or a goals-based peace ends both sides' battles, sends troops back to controllable territory and starts a truce lasting [[turn:{{days}}]]. If there is nowhere to withdraw to, troops are reorganized or disbanded and the corresponding manpower is recovered.
guide.step.aiOpponent.title: AI Opponents
guide.step.aiOpponent.body: The computer builds its economy, raises troops, prepares diplomatic projects, contests provinces with province armies, enforces war goals and sues for peace. Watch the target nation details in the diplomacy panel, your army units at the top right and the war log to judge pressure on each front.
guide.section.world.label: Seasons & Victory
guide.section.world.lead: The four seasons affect movement and combat; the capital is a vital objective, but capturing it does not win the war on its own.
guide.step.seasons.title: Four Seasons & Snow
guide.step.seasons.body: The season changes every [[turn:{{days}}]]. Winter snow slows marches and weakens offensives, with deeper snow hitting harder — a good time to switch to defense and recovery.
guide.step.victory.title: Victory Conditions
guide.step.victory.body: Eliminate every rival through war goals and formal-territory settlements to be the last nation standing and win. The fall of your own capital does not immediately defeat you or automatically annex all your land; keep defending formal territory, counterattack or make peace. A capital is a high-output core city with a strong [[garrison]], a key source of [[supply]], and a major condition for full annexation.
guide.step.warReport.title: War Log
guide.step.warReport.body: The live war log above the map pushes battles, occupations, diplomacy and season news in a compact Nation + Action + Target format, with nation names colour-tagged and positive/negative values in green/red; entries fade out automatically, and clicking the arrow expands the full history so you can review the campaign.
